text: A Gaussian beam is focused to a smaller waist radius w₀. What happens to its far-field divergence angle θ?
choices: It decreases, because a tighter focus stays collimated longer
It increases, because the product w₀θ = λ/π is fixed
It is unchanged, because divergence is independent of waist
It becomes zero, because the beam is diffraction-limited
explanation: For any Gaussian beam w₀θ = λ/π is a constant (the diffraction-limited 'uncertainty product'), so a smaller waist forces a larger divergence θ = λ/(πw₀). Believing a tighter focus reduces divergence, or that divergence is waist-independent or exactly zero, contradicts this fixed product.
